observation.visible_scene: A close-up view of a sunset (or sunrise) sky filled with layered clouds. A bright orange glow dominates the upper-left, while a diagonal band of lit cloud runs from the top-center down toward the lower-right. The right side and lower-middle are occupied by darker purple and mauve cloud banks, with thin orange wisps glowing through gaps near the bottom. No sun disk, horizon, or ground is visible; the entire frame is cloud texture.
visible_changes: Across the excerpt the cloud formations drift and morph very slowly; differences between consecutive frames are small, indicating gentle motion rather than rapid change.
The bright orange patch in the upper-left gradually softens and its boundary with the purple sky shifts slightly inward over time.
The illuminated diagonal band in the center subtly changes shape and brightness, with the orange wisps in the lower-middle appearing to reconfigure.
The dark purple cloud mass along the right edge appears to advance/expand a little leftward as the clip progresses.
Overall color balance slowly deepens toward purple on the right while orange at lower-center remains glowing, consistent with ongoing light change on moving clouds.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the cloud drift and color shift continue, reverse, or stabilize after t=3.2s is unknown.
The cause of the lighting trend (sun setting, sun rising, or cloud shadowing) is not shown.
What lies above, below, or beyond the frame edges is unseen.
uncertain_details: The apparent slow shift of the whole cloud field cannot be cleanly separated into camera pan/zoom versus actual cloud translation; background evidence is insufficient to confirm camera motion.
Exact speed and direction of individual cloud features are hard to quantify given the subtle frame-to-frame changes.
Whether the darkening on the right is cloud movement into frame or a change in illumination is ambiguous.
